events.headline: Cam Skattebo (hamstring) inactive at Philadelphia; Devin Singletary is the lead back
events.detail: The Giants made Skattebo inactive for the 1:00 p.m. ET game at Philadelphia after he was listed doubtful Friday. Tyrone Tracy Jr. is on IR, so Devin Singletary is the primary back.
events.so_what: Skattebo is out: get him out of any lineup. Devin Singletary is a volume FLEX start this week; he only becomes a Tuesday bid if Skattebo misses Week 10 too.

source.label: PhillyVoice: Eagles-Giants Week 9 inactives (Nov. 8)

events.headline: George Pickens (hamstring) inactive at Indianapolis; Jake Ferguson active
events.detail: Dallas made George Pickens inactive after he played through the hamstring last week. Jake Ferguson (ankle) is active despite not practicing until a limited Friday session. KaVontae Turpin is also inactive, which pushes Ryan Flournoy into a featured slot role beside CeeDee Lamb.
events.so_what: Bench Pickens now, before the 1 p.m. ET lock. Ferguson is active, so start him at a TE position this shallow, accepting some snap risk. CeeDee Lamb gets a target bump; Ryan Flournoy is a deep-league FLEX only if you are short a body.

source.label: NBC Sports: George Pickens inactive for Week 9 against Colts (Nov. 8)

events.headline: Amon-Ra St. Brown active at Miami, off the Lions inactive list
events.detail: Detroit's inactives at Miami are Cade Mays, DJ Wonnum, D.J. Reed, Jacob Saylors, Jackson Meeks, Ahmed Hassanein and Mekhi Wingo. St. Brown, questionable with a rib injury after three limited practices, is not among them. Sione Vaki is also active and backs up Jahmyr Gibbs with Saylors out.
events.so_what: Amon-Ra St. Brown is active: start him as a WR1. Jahmyr Gibbs is unaffected; Saylors being out does not change his workload.

source.label: Yahoo Sports: Lions, Dolphins Week 9 inactives (Nov. 8)

events.headline: Brian Robinson Jr. (hamstring) placed on IR; Khalil Herbert promoted behind Bijan Robinson
events.detail: Atlanta put Robinson on IR Saturday after he missed two games with a lingering hamstring injury, per ESPN's Marc Raimondi via RotoWire. He must miss at least four more games, with mid-December the earliest return. The Falcons promoted Khalil Herbert from the practice squad as the No. 2 back.
events.so_what: Bijan Robinson's workload was already secure and this removes his only real competition for touches. Brian Robinson Jr. is an IR stash at most; Herbert is a handcuff for Bijan managers only, not a FAAB bid.

source.label: RotoWire: Brian Robinson placed on injured reserve (Nov. 7)

events.headline: Pat Bryant activated from IR but still questionable at Carolina; Sean Payton says he is in line to play
events.detail: Denver activated Bryant Saturday, per RotoWire. He sprained his right ankle and was carted off in Week 4 at San Francisco, went on IR before Week 5, and practiced fully all week after being designated to return Wednesday. He keeps a questionable tag, but Payton told The Denver Gazette on Friday that he expects him to play. Kickoff is 1:00 p.m. ET.
events.so_what: A first game back after five weeks out is a bench-and-watch, not a start. His snap share Sunday decides whether he is worth a Week 10 FLEX look in a Broncos receiver room that has rotated without him.

source.label: RotoWire: Pat Bryant activated from IR (Nov. 7)

events.headline: D.J. Moore and Keon Coleman cleared, no designation for Monday at Minnesota; Joshua Palmer ruled out
events.detail: Moore (shoulder) was limited all week and still wore a non-contact jersey Saturday, as he has since an AC joint sprain in Week 2, but carries no game status, per RotoWire. Coleman (shoulder) is also clear. Palmer (hamstring) will not play. Moore has 16 catches for 260 yards and two touchdowns on 27 targets in five games.
events.so_what: Moore plays and is a FLEX-range receiver against a Minnesota team starting Carson Wentz. Palmer's absence concentrates the targets on Moore, Coleman and the tight ends.

source.label: RotoWire: DJ Moore in clear for Week 9 (Nov. 7)

events.headline: Christian Kirk to IR, Demarcus Robinson activated and cleared; Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel out vs. the Raiders
events.detail: San Francisco placed Kirk on IR with a meniscus injury Saturday and activated Robinson (ankle), who no longer carries a designation, per RotoWire. Evans (Achilles, aggravated in Week 6) misses a third straight game and Samuel (hamstring) is out, per ESPN's Nick Wagoner. The active receivers are Robinson, Jordan Watkins, Brandin Cooks and Jacob Cowing. Separately, Brandon Aiyuk met with the 49ers and his agent Friday after filing reinstatement paperwork in late October, saying he is healthy; roughly $13 million in forfeited bonuses could push it to arbitration, and the team could release, trade or roster him, per RotoWire (Nov. 7).
events.so_what: Bench Evans and Samuel. Kirk is out at least four games. The thin receiver room should funnel touches to the backfield and tight end, and no 49ers fill-in receiver is worth a bid on a depleted room. Aiyuk is a speculative stash only where a bench slot is free; nothing is resolved and he may never play for San Francisco.

source.label: 49ers lose WR Christian Kirk to IR; activate WR Demarcus Robinson (Nov. 7)

events.headline: A.J. Brown and TreVeyon Henderson ruled out vs. Green Bay; Hunter Henry questionable after a limited Friday
events.detail: Friday's final report rules out Brown (ankle, knee) and Henderson (illness). Henry (foot) sat the first two practices, returned limited Friday and is questionable; Patriots.com expects New England to lean on rookie Eli Raridon at tight end. Rhamondre Stevenson is not on the report and leads the backfield with Corey Kiner as the spell back. Mack Hollins (calf) came off IR Saturday and is questionable; he led New England in catches and yards when he went down four games ago, per Pro Football Rumors. Henderson said in a Friday statement, per Pro Football Rumors, that he was hospitalized for several days with unexplained neurological symptoms affecting his strength and coordination; there is no return timeline.
events.so_what: Bench Brown. Henderson is an indefinite absence rather than a one-week illness, so he is an IR stash where you have the slot and Stevenson is a confident RB2/FLEX start on volume for the foreseeable future. Henry is a genuine coin flip resolved at Sunday inactives; if you roster him, have Raridon or a streaming tight end ready.

source.label: Patriots.com: Patriots rule out A.J. Brown, TreVeyon Henderson; Hunter Henry questionable (Nov. 6)

events.headline: Jordyn Tyson activated from IR and expected to debut vs. Cleveland, still questionable and likely on a pitch count
events.detail: The Saints activated Tyson Saturday, per RotoWire, and Jordan Schultz reports he intends to make his NFL debut Sunday. He never reached a full practice this week and keeps a questionable tag, so Pro Football Rumors expects a cautious first game. LT Kelvin Banks is also being activated. Travis Etienne Jr.'s window has not opened, CJ Donaldson (shoulder, concussion) is out, Alvin Kamara (back) is cleared, and the Saints waived Kendre Miller.
events.so_what: Tyson is a bench-and-watch in his first game back from a season-long hamstring issue; his snap share Sunday decides whether he is a Week 10 start. Donaldson out and Etienne not back leave Kamara and Audric Estime as the backfield, and Estime is a cheap add only if he gets the clear No. 2 role Sunday.

source.label: Pro Football Rumors: Saints to activate WR Jordyn Tyson, LT Kelvin Banks (Nov. 7)

events.headline: No team close to the Colts' Jonathan Taylor price; Titans plan to keep Tony Pollard; Josh Downs draws a fourth-round offer
events.detail: Per The Ringer's Tom Pelissero via Pro Football Rumors, nobody has come close to Indianapolis' first-round-equivalent ask for Taylor; the best known offer is a second plus another pick. The Giants led Friday, but PFR now calls Indianapolis keeping him "firmly in play," while The Athletic's Jonathan Jones still expects a trade, with Denver, Green Bay, Seattle and Minnesota also in the mix. Downs, who requested a trade, has at least one offer including a fourth (Schefter, Rapoport); the Colts reportedly want a third and Kansas City is the suitor named most. Keenan Allen is also drawing interest, and several teams have called about Jones. The deadline is Tuesday, Nov. 10. Tennessee has not received a viable offer for Pollard and plans to keep him to support Cam Ward, per Pro Football Rumors (Nov. 7); SI's Albert Breer says buyers believe a fourth-round pick is the floor, and Pollard (595 rushing yards, six TDs) becomes a fallback target if Taylor does not move. Calvin Ridley, with six catches this year, is the Titan most likely to be dealt.
events.so_what: Taylor stays a start while he is a Colt; a move to New York would split work with Cam Skattebo and hurt Skattebo first. Seth McGowan is the Colts back to own the moment a deal is official. Downs is a slot receiver whose value depends on the landing spot, so hold him through Tuesday. Any Jones exit opens Anthony Richardson, whose rushing scores at running-back rates under the konami premium. Pollard is a volume start in Tennessee and staying put is the good outcome for him; a trade into a committee would be the risk.

source.label: Pro Football Rumors: No team coming close to Colts' Jonathan Taylor price (Nov. 7)

events.headline: Jauan Jennings (calf) ruled out for Monday night vs. Buffalo
events.detail: Kevin O'Connell said Jennings hurt the calf at Thursday's practice and that it is serious enough to sideline him for at least one game, per RotoWire. Tai Felton and Myles Price pick up snaps behind Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison, with Carson Wentz at quarterback. Jennings' next chance to play is Week 10 at Green Bay.
events.so_what: Bench him now rather than waiting for Monday; a Sunday receiver in his slot is the safe swap. Felton and Price are one-week fill-ins in a Wentz offense, not FAAB targets.

source.label: RotoWire: Jauan Jennings won't play in Week 9 (Nov. 7)

events.headline: Kyler Murray (hamstring) out Monday vs. Buffalo with a Grade 2 strain that may cost more than one week; Carson Wentz starts
events.detail: Kevin O'Connell ruled Murray out Thursday and called him week-to-week, with IR not under consideration, per ESPN. Netflix's Tom Pelissero reported Saturday, via RotoWire, that it is a Grade 2 hamstring strain that will keep him out Monday "and potentially beyond." Wentz starts with Max Brosmer behind him and may start past Monday.
events.so_what: Murray is a bench and the rushing premium goes with him, likely for Week 10 at Green Bay as well. Wentz is a pocket passer, so the Minnesota receivers keep their volume but lose some ceiling. Wentz is a streaming option at most.

source.label: RotoWire: Kyler Murray dealing with Grade 2 strain (Nov. 7)

events.headline: Deshaun Watson clears concussion protocol but Shedeur Sanders starts at New Orleans
events.detail: Watson cleared the protocol Saturday and is questionable, but Todd Monken told the Browns' Kelsey Russo that Sanders starts Sunday, per RotoWire. Watson could be the active backup or the emergency third quarterback. Sanders started seven games as a rookie in 2025 with 1,400 yards, seven touchdowns and 10 interceptions.
events.so_what: Watson is a bench this week whatever his status. Sanders has some konami value on scrambles, but his rookie turnover rate makes him a deep streamer at best, with INTs costing only -1 the one comfort. Lower the Cleveland receivers; Quinshon Judkins holds up best if the game stays close, and Harold Fannin Jr. is the most reliable pass catcher.

source.label: RotoWire: Deshaun Watson clears concussion protocol, still questionable (Nov. 7)

events.headline: Malik Nabers cleared, no designation for Sunday at Philadelphia after a full Friday practice
events.detail: Nabers (knee) missed Thursday, then was a full participant Friday and has no game status on the Giants' final report.
events.so_what: Start him as usual; the full Friday answers the question Thursday's DNP raised.

source.label: Giants.com: Giants vs. Eagles Week 9 injury report (Nov. 6)

events.headline: DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) ruled out vs. the Giants; Smith not expected back until Week 11
events.detail: Both miss a third straight game. NBC Sports Philadelphia says Smith will not return until at least Week 11, after the bye. Joe Milton's receivers are Makai Lemon, Darius Cooper, Hollywood Brown and Elijah Moore.
events.so_what: Bench Smith and plan around two more weeks without him. No single Eagles receiver has claimed the role, and a Milton-led passing game is not a reason to spend FAAB on any of them.

source.label: NBC Sports Philadelphia: DeVonta Smith among those ruled out vs. NYG (Nov. 6)

events.headline: Ravens finalize the Jacoby Brissett trade after Joe Fagnano throws for 60 yards and two INTs in a 33-10 loss
events.detail: The trade became official Friday, per Pro Football Rumors; Arizona restructured Brissett to a one-year, $15.5 million deal to make it work, and Baltimore waived Austin Reed. Brissett could start as soon as Week 10 against the Chargers; the Ravens had not named him the starter when this was checked. Fagnano went 10 of 18 for 60 yards and two interceptions Thursday in his first NFL start, with Lamar Jackson (thumb, IR) and Tyler Huntley (out for the year) unavailable, and Zay Flowers caught three passes for six yards. A Henry trade out of Baltimore is unlikely before Tuesday's deadline, per RotoWire (Nov. 7), and Lamar Jackson's return from thumb surgery depends on his recovery and the team's playoff position.
events.so_what: Nothing in this passing game was startable with Fagnano. A Brissett start in Week 10 restores Flowers as a weekly start and Mark Andrews as a TD-capable tight end; confirm he is named before moving either back into a lineup. Henry stays a volume back facing loaded boxes and is staying put, so he is a volume start until a passer settles in.

source.label: Pro Football Rumors: Ravens finalize trade for Cardinals QB Jacoby Brissett (Nov. 6)

events.headline: Saquon Barkley cleared, no designation for Sunday vs. the Giants after two limited practices
events.detail: Barkley (hamstring, back) missed Wednesday, then was limited Thursday and Friday and carries no game status on the final report; NBC Sports Philadelphia says he is expected to play. He played 22 snaps to Elijah Mitchell's 39 in Week 8. Joe Milton starts at quarterback with Tanner McKee (rib) questionable.
events.so_what: He plays, but two capped practices and last week's 22 snaps keep Mitchell involved, so he is a flex-range start in this 2-FLEX format rather than an RB1 anchor. Mitchell stays a bench hold, not a Tuesday bid.

source.label: NBC Sports Philadelphia: DeVonta Smith among those ruled out vs. NYG (Nov. 6)

events.headline: Garrett Wilson (concussion) ruled out at Kansas City; Adonai Mitchell steps into the top receiver role
events.detail: The Jets ruled Wilson out Friday after he entered the protocol Monday following a Week 8 helmet-to-helmet hit. Mason Taylor (back) was limited Wednesday and full Thursday and carries no Out tag.
events.so_what: Bench Wilson. Mitchell and Taylor absorb the targets for one week against Kansas City; that is a one-week bump, not a FAAB-worthy role change unless Wilson's protocol drags into Week 10.

source.label: Arrowhead Pride via Yahoo: Chiefs-Jets Week 9 final injury report (Nov. 6)

events.headline: Emeka Egbuka (foot) questionable for Sunday night at Chicago despite full Thursday and Friday practices
events.detail: Egbuka missed Wednesday, then was full Thursday and Friday, and Tampa Bay still listed him questionable. Gainwell (hip) was limited Wednesday, full the next two days and carries no status. Chris Godwin Jr. and Bucky Irving returned to full practice Friday after Thursday rest days. Kickoff is 8:20 p.m. ET Sunday.
events.so_what: Two full practices make Egbuka a likely start, and the night kickoff lets you confirm at 6:50 p.m. ET inactives. If you roster him, keep a Sunday-night or Monday WR on the bench as the swap.

source.label: Buccaneers.com: Buccaneers-Bears injury report Nov. 6 (Nov. 6)

events.headline: Bam Knight (concussion) ruled out at Seattle; Tyler Allgeier leads Arizona with Jeremiyah Love on IR
events.detail: Mike LaFleur ruled out Knight, plus guards Jon Gaines II and Jayden Williams, on Friday. Love is on IR with a high-ankle sprain (4 to 5 weeks). Allgeier is the lead back.
events.so_what: Allgeier is a volume FLEX start this week behind a line missing two starters. With Love out for weeks, he is the FAAB target in this backfield if still on your wire; James Conner is the handcuff behind him.

source.label: Heavy: Seahawks get injury boost as Cardinals rule out 3 players (Nov. 6)

events.headline: Christian Watson cleared, no designation for Sunday at New England
events.detail: Watson (rib) was limited all week and has no game status on the Packers' final report; Packers.com expects him available. Josh Whyle (concussion) and Micah Parsons (knee) are out, and Chris Brooks (ankle) is questionable and must be activated from IR.
events.so_what: Watson plays, which caps Matthew Golden's target share. A limited rib week argues for a FLEX slot rather than a WR2 lock.

source.label: Packers.com: Packers list three questionable, rule out five vs. Patriots (Nov. 6)

events.headline: Drew Lock cleared, no designation, starts vs. Arizona with Sam Darnold out; Rashid Shaheed ruled out
events.detail: Lock (right elbow) was limited all three practice days and has no game status for Sunday, per John Boyle via RotoWire; he replaces Darnold (quad, cracked rib) for at least one game, with Jalen Milroe the backup. Mike Macdonald called Darnold week to week but he is not going on IR. Lock went 35 of 48 for 422 yards, four touchdowns and no interceptions across Weeks 1 and 2, including a start at Arizona. Shaheed (knee) will not play.
events.so_what: Lock is a matchup streamer against a defense he already beat, with the elbow the reason not to trust him over an established starter. Jaxon Smith-Njigba stays a start, since his target volume does not depend on who is throwing. Bench Shaheed. Milroe is a deep konami stash only if Darnold misses more time and the elbow goes wrong.

source.label: RotoWire: Drew Lock set for Week 9 start (Nov. 6)

events.headline: Christian McCaffrey cleared, no designation for Sunday vs. the Raiders
events.detail: McCaffrey (left hamstring) has no game status after limited practices Thursday and Friday, per ESPN's Nick Wagoner via RotoWire. The hamstring limited him to a season-low 52 percent of snaps at Atlanta in Week 7, when he still produced 100 scrimmage yards and a rushing touchdown on 13 touches.
events.so_what: Start him. With Evans, Samuel and Kirk all out, the offense runs through him. Two limited days leave a small chance of a reduced snap share, so Kaelon Black stays the handcuff to keep, not a cut.

source.label: RotoWire: Christian McCaffrey set to play Sunday (Nov. 6)

events.headline: Breece Hall practices fully Thursday and Friday and is set to return at Kansas City; Glenn says "both will play" with Braelon Allen
events.detail: Hall was full on Thursday and Friday and is returning this week, per Arrowhead Pride's final Chiefs-Jets report; The Athletic's Zack Rosenblatt (via RotoBaller) reported Hall saying he is ready after five missed games. Aaron Glenn has said both he and Allen will play. Allen has run for more than 500 yards in relief.
events.so_what: Hall plays, but a back returning from five missed games into a stated split is a FLEX, not an RB1, until the snap counts say otherwise. Allen keeps standalone value as the back with the current role.

source.label: Arrowhead Pride via Yahoo: Chiefs-Jets Week 9 final injury report (Nov. 6)

events.headline: David Montgomery (groin) ruled out for Week 9 and week-to-week; Woody Marks starts at the Chargers
events.detail: DeMeco Ryans ruled Montgomery out Wednesday, his third straight miss since the Week 5 injury, and called him week-to-week, per NBC Sports. Montgomery has 138 rushing yards at 2.7 a carry this year. Marks had 19 carries for 66 yards and a 15-yard catch against the Giants in Week 7, and 15 carries for 56 and two catches for 25 against Jacksonville. Houston comes off a Week 8 bye.
events.so_what: Marks is a volume RB2/FLEX with a poor per-carry rate, so his value is the workload and TD chances rather than yards. Montgomery is a bench hold, with a Week 10 return uncertain. Don't overpay to add a backup in this running game.

source.label: NBC Sports: Ryans says Montgomery (groin) will not play in Week 9 (Nov. 4)
